ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23/r1.claim: The address reminds all people that they need God's generosity and blessing in every state, while He alone is absolutely independent of creation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23/r1.anchor: وأن جميع الناس محتاجون إلى إحسان الله تعالى وإنعامه في جميع أحوالهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23/r2.claim: Calling humanity الفقراء makes their intense need vivid by treating the whole human race as the class of the poor; الغني is paired with it and الحميد marks God as generous and worthy of praise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23/r2.anchor: وعرف الفقراء ليريهم شديد افتقارهم إليه

STUDYQURAN:35:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:intro/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:35:intro/r6.claim: The sūrah’s main focus is God’s oneness as the sole Creator and Sustainer, contrasting divine Power with claims made for idols.
STUDYQURAN:35:intro/r6.anchor: The main focus of the sūrah is upon the Oneness of God as the only Creator and Sustainer of existence

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r6.claim: The people of Sheba exemplify nations that answer divine favors with arrogance and disorder, then face exemplary punishment and lose those favors.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r6.anchor: nations who after being bestowed with God’s favours become arrogant and spread anarchy in the land instead of becoming grateful are punished by God in an exemplary manner.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r7.claim: The people of Sheba fulfilled Satan's prediction and were deprived of God's favors, becoming a tale of the ancients.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r7.anchor: The people of Sabā’ fulfilled the prediction of Satan about them.

RAZI-FULL:v26p12#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#3/r1.claim: Against disbelievers who suggested God urgently commands worship because He needs it, Rāzī says worship is commanded for human care, not divine need.
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#3/r1.anchor: لما كثر الدعاء من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والإصرار من الكفار

RAZI-FULL:v26p12#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#3/r2.claim: Although predicates are usually indefinite, a definite predicate is apt when both facts are known and the statement reminds rather than informs; everyone already knows humans are needy.
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#3/r2.anchor: فإن كان الخبر معلوما عند السامع والمبتدأ كذلك ويقع الخبر تنبيها لا تفهيما يحسن تعريف الخبر غاية الحسن

RAZI-FULL:v26p12#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#3/r3.claim: The phrase teaches that dependence and reliance belong to God alone, requiring worship of Him and excluding worship of anything on which people do not depend.
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#3/r3.anchor: إعلام بأنه لا افتقار إلا إليه ولا اتكال إلا عليه وهذا يوجب عبادته لكونه مفتقرا إليه وعدم عبادة غيره لعدم الافتقار إلى غيره

RAZI-FULL:v26p12#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#3/r4.claim: Though wholly self-sufficient, God calls people repeatedly, while they remain needy yet fail to answer or call upon Him for a response.
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#3/r4.anchor: أي هو مع استغنائه يدعوكم كل الدعاء وأنتم من احتياجكم لا تجيبونه ولا تدعونه فيجيبكم

RAZI-FULL:v26p12#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#3/r5.claim: Adding “to God” emphasizes exclusive worship; adding “Praiseworthy” to “rich” signals that His favors merit gratitude and worship.
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#3/r5.anchor: إشارة لوجوب حصر العبادة في عبادته

RAZI-FULL:v26p12#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#3/r6.claim: Human poverty is not matched by divine poverty: God is absolutely rich, meets people’s worldly needs, and will meet believers’ needs in the next life.

STUDYQURAN:35:15/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:15/r1.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:35:15/r1.claim: In Sufi thought, humans are wholly poor before God and depend on Him for existence and sustenance, while God is wholly self-sufficient.
STUDYQURAN:35:15/r1.anchor: with regard to being both brought into existence and provided sustenance (Aj).

STUDYQURAN:35:15/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:15/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:35:15/r2.claim: Realizing God's fullness or richness depends on realizing one's complete poverty before Him.
STUDYQURAN:35:15/r2.anchor: realizing the Fullness or Richness of God depends upon the realization of one’s complete poverty before God.

STUDYQURAN:35:15/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:15/r3.speaker: al-Tustarī
STUDYQURAN:35:15/r3.claim: Al-Tustarī says God ordained servants' poverty in relation to Him; claiming wealth veils one from God, while acknowledging poverty joins the servant's poverty to God's wealth.
STUDYQURAN:35:15/r3.anchor: As al-Tustarī writes,“You [depend] upon Him in your very selves, for when God created creation, He ordained

STUDYQURAN:35:15/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:15/r4.speaker: al-Tustarī
STUDYQURAN:35:15/r4.claim: The servant should feel inward poverty and cut off all besides God so servanthood is pure humility and abasement.
STUDYQURAN:35:15/r4.anchor: As al-Tustarī writes,“You [depend] upon Him in your very selves

STUDYQURAN:35:15/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:15/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:35:15/r5.claim: Need for God is intrinsic to human nature, while need for other things is accidental; one should turn away from all besides God.
STUDYQURAN:35:15/r5.anchor: poverty toward and need for God is intrinsic to human nature, whereas poverty toward or need for other things is accidental.

STUDYQURAN:35:15/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:15/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:35:15/r6.claim: Every experienced need is ultimately a need for God, since the things needed both veil Him and reveal Him.
STUDYQURAN:35:15/r6.anchor: every need that one experiences is ultimately a need for God, since the phenomena for which one experiences need are veils that hide God and also reveal God.

STUDYQURAN:35:15/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:15/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:35:15/r7.claim: God's being praised is intrinsic to the Divine Nature and does not depend on anyone praising Him.
STUDYQURAN:35:15/r7.anchor: being praised is intrinsic to the Divine Nature and not dependent upon anything to praise Him.

STUDYQURAN:35:15/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:15/r8.speaker: al-Maybudī
STUDYQURAN:35:15/r8.claim: Al-Maybudī says only those who fully realize their poverty truly praise God.
STUDYQURAN:35:15/r8.anchor: al-Maybudī states that only those who fully realize poverty truly praise God.

BURSEVI:v7p260/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p260/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p260/r1.claim: Faqir is linked to breaking a vertebra; Taj al-Masadir derives the verb from the pattern of daraba, while al-Qamus assigns it to the pattern of karuma.
BURSEVI:v7p260/r1.anchor: ذكره في "تاج المصادر" في باب ضرب وجعله في "القاموس" من حد كرم

BURSEVI:v7p260/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p260/r2.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v7p260/r2.claim: Al-Raghib says one says iftaqara, muftaqir, and faqir; faqara is rarely used although the analogy would allow it.
BURSEVI:v7p260/r2.anchor: يقال افتقر فهو مفتقر وفقير ولا يكاد يقال فقر وإن كان القياس يقتضيه

BURSEVI:v7p260/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p260/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p260/r3.claim: Faqir is an intensive form for one in great and severe need; the definite plural emphasizes that people alone are the truly needy, making other kinds of need negligible by comparison.
BURSEVI:v7p260/r3.anchor: وفهم من هذا أن الفقير صيغة مبالغة كالمفتقر بمعنى ذي الاحتياج الكثير والشديد

BURSEVI:v7p260/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p260/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p260/r4.claim: People need God intensely in themselves and every serious affair: each created thing needs its creator to originate and sustain it, while people need worldly provision and protection and forgiveness in the hereafter.
BURSEVI:v7p260/r4.anchor: كل حادث مفتقر إلى خالقه ليبديه وينشئه أولا ويديمه ويبقيه ثانيا

BURSEVI:v7p260/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p260/r5.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v7p260/r5.claim: Some Sufi authorities say humanity alone receives the direct address “poor to God”: creatures need God's acts, but humans need God's essence and attributes.
BURSEVI:v7p260/r5.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : إن الله تعالى ما شرف شيئا من المخلوقات بتشريف خطاب أنتم الفقراء

BURSEVI:v7p260/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p260/r6.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v7p260/r6.claim: He compares creatures dependent on God's treasury to subjects dependent on a ruler's stores, while lovers depend on the ruler's own person and attributes.
BURSEVI:v7p260/r6.anchor: كمثل سلطان له رعية وهو صاحب جمال فيكون افتقار جميع رعاياه إلى خزائنه وممالكه ويكون افتقار عشقاه إلى عين ذاته وصفاته

BURSEVI:v7p261/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p261/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p261/r1.claim: God alone is absolutely self-sufficient; all others need Him, while even a ruler needs servants and a merchant needs carriers, and God needs no helpers or anything else.
BURSEVI:v7p261/r1.anchor: المستغني على الإطلاق فكل أحد يحتاج إليه لأن أحدا

BURSEVI:v7p261/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p261/r2.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
BURSEVI:v7p261/r2.claim: God is independent of creation: creating them or not, keeping them alive, and charging them or not charging them are all alike to Him.
BURSEVI:v7p261/r2.anchor: معناه الغني عن خلقه فلو لم يخلقهم لجاز ولو أدام حياتهم لابتلاهم كلفهم أو لم يكلفهم فالكل عنده بمثابة واحدة

BURSEVI:v7p261/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p261/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p261/r3.claim: The author rejects the Mu'tazili claim that God would not be wise unless He charged people to know and thank Him; that claim makes creation serve a benefit or avert harm.
BURSEVI:v7p261/r3.anchor: خلافا للمعتزلة حيث قالوا : لو لم يكلفهم معرفته وشكره لم يكن حكيما وهذا غاية الخزي ويفضي إلى القول بأن خلقهم لنفع أو دفع

BURSEVI:v7p261/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p261/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p261/r4.claim: He equates the idea that God created beings to protect Himself from harm with the Magian claim that angels were created to shield Him from Satan.
BURSEVI:v7p261/r4.anchor: حيث زعموا وقالوا : خلق الله الملائكة ليدفع بهم عن نفسه أذى الشيطان

BURSEVI:v7p261/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p261/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p261/r5.claim: God is praised because He grants blessings to all beings through His universal favor; He is the self-sufficient giver of sufficiency.
BURSEVI:v7p261/r5.anchor: المنعم على جميع الموجودات حتى استحق عليهم الحمد على نعمته العامة وفضله الشامل فالله الغني المغني

BURSEVI:v7p261/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p261/r6.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v7p261/r6.claim: Al-Kashifi reads possible essences' need for an agent as human poverty, God's essential perfection as His independence, and the manifestation of divine names through created beings as a great favor deserving praise.
BURSEVI:v7p261/r6.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (ببايد دانست كه ماهيات ممكنه در وجود محتاجند بفاعل

TAB-FULL:v19p352/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p352/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p352/r1.claim: Humans depend on God and should worship and seek His pleasure; He has no need of their worship or service, and meets their needs.

TAB-FULL:v19p352/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p352/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p352/r2.claim: God has no need of human worship, service, or anything from people or anyone else.

TAB-FULL:v19p352/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p352/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p352/r3.claim: Al-Ḥamīd means the One praised for His blessings; every blessing belongs to Him, so praise and thanks are due to Him in every circumstance.
TAB-FULL:v19p352/r3.anchor: {الحميد} [إبراهيم: 1] يعني: المحمود على نعمه، فإن كل نعمة بكم وبغيركم فمنه، فله الحمد والشكر بكل حال

TABATABAI:35:15-16/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:15-16/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:15-16/r1.claim: After showing that creation and governance belong to God and alleged gods own nothing, the passage adds a warning: God needs no people, while they need him, and he can replace them if he wills as recompense for their deeds.
TABATABAI:35:15-16/r1.anchor: أخذ يبين ذلك ببيان آخر مشوب بالوعيد والتهديد وهو أنه تعالى غني عنهم وهم فقراء إليه فله أن يذهبهم

TABATABAI:35:15-16/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:15-16/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:15-16/r3.claim: The deniers’ conduct suggests that they imagine they can become independent of God through idol worship and that God needs them; the verse refutes this by restricting all poverty to people and all richness to God.
TABATABAI:35:15-16/r3.anchor: السياق يشعر بأن أعمال هؤلاء المكذبين كانت تكشف عن أنهم كانوا يتوهمون أن لهم أن يستغنوا عن الله سبحانه بعبادة آلهتهم

TABATABAI:35:15-16/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:15-16/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:15-16/r4.claim: Because richness and poverty mean possession and lack and cannot both be absent, the exclusive wording implies that people have only poverty while God has only richness.
TABATABAI:35:15-16/r4.anchor: وإذ كان الغنى والفقر وهما الوجدان والفقدان متقابلين لا يرتفعان عن موضوعهما كان لازم القصر السابق قصر آخر

TABATABAI:35:15-16/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:15-16/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:15-16/r5.claim: God is rich in himself and can dispense with or replace people, while they are inherently unable to dispense with him; his creation and management ground this asymmetry, and he is praised in those acts.
TABATABAI:35:15-16/r5.anchor: والملاك في غناه تعالى عنهم وفقرهم أنه تعالى خالقهم ومدبر أمرهم

TABATABAI:35:15-16/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:15-16/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:15-16/r6.claim: Although the verse addresses people, the universal cause—dependence on the creator and manager—extends the judgment to all creatures, whether people means deniers specifically or humankind generally.
TABATABAI:35:15-16/r6.anchor: وذلك أن عموم علة الحكم يعمم الحكم فكأنه قيل أنتم معاشر الخليقة الفقراء إلى خالقكم المدبر لأمركم

TABRISI:35:11-17/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:11-17/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:35:11-17/r14.claim: People are needy before God, while He has no need of their worship.
TABRISI:35:11-17/r14.anchor: { إلى الله والله هو الغني } عن عبادتكم لا يحتاج إلى شيء

TABRISI:35:11-17/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:11-17/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:35:11-17/r15.claim: God deserves praise for all His acts and does only what merits praise.
TABRISI:35:11-17/r15.anchor: المستحق للحمد على جميع أفعاله فلا يفعل إلا ما يستحق به حمدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p413/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p413/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p413/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the people addressed here are the people of Mecca.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p413/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد أهل مكة (¬3).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p413/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p413/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p413/r2.claim: People need God's provision and forgiveness; He has no need of their worship and is praiseworthy with or without His creatures.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p413/r2.anchor: {أنتم الفقراء إلى الله} المحتاجون إلى رزقه ومغفرته. (وهو الغني) عن عبادتكم {الحميد} إلى خلقه وغير خلقه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r4.claim: Humanity is in need of God, while He is independent of them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r4.anchor: {يأيها الناس أنتم الفقراء إلى الله والله هو الغني} [فاطر: 15] عنكم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r5.claim: God is praiseworthy by His creatures and has made them duty-bound to praise Him.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r5.anchor: {الحميد} [فاطر: 15] المستحمد إلى خلقه، استوجب عليهم أن يحمدوه

ELMALILI:35:15-22/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r1.claim: The definite predicate expresses restriction: religion and worship meet human need, not any need of God's.
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r1.anchor: أَنتُمُ ٱلْفُقَرَآءُ cümlesinde müsnedin ta‘rîfi kasr ifade eder. Yani din ve ibadet Allah’ın ihtiyâcı değil, insanların ihtiyâcıdır.

ELMALILI:35:15-22/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r2.claim: Humans are the creatures most in need of God: created weak and bearing the trust, the human soul has needs unmatched by other creatures.
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r2.anchor: Hem mahlûkāt içinde Allah’a ihtiyâcı en çok olan fukarâ, sade insanlardır.

ELMALILI:35:15-22/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r3.claim: Only God can satisfy human need; there is no other deity to worship.
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r3.anchor: İnsanın bu ihtiyâcını tatmin etmek için de Allah’tan başka mâbud bulunmaz.

ELMALILI:35:15-22/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r4.claim: God is truly rich and entirely independent, needing nothing.
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r4.anchor: Ganî O hiçbir ihtiyâcı olmayan ve her şeyden müstağnî, tam mânasıyla zengin, Ganî O, yalnız O’dur.

ELMALILI:35:15-22/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r5.claim: Others own not even a qitmir, while God is able to satisfy every need and does not depend on human worship.
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r5.anchor: Ganî O hiçbir ihtiyâcı olmayan ve her şeyden müstağnî

ELMALILI:35:15-22/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r6.claim: God does not need worship and has the power to meet all human needs.
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r6.anchor: O sizin ibadetinize muhtaç olmadığı gibi bütün ihtiyaçlarınızı tatmin edebilecek kudrete de mâliktir

ELMALILI:35:15-22/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r7.claim: God alone is the praised benefactor who deserves gratitude, worship, and honor and grants requests.
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r7.anchor: Onun için dileklerinizi verirse ancak O verir, hem O kendisine hamd ettirmesini bilir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:15/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:15/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:15/r1.claim: God created humanity and knows its needs: people need God, while God needs nothing and no one.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:15/r1.anchor: Allah’a muhtaç olan insanlardır, Allah ise hiçbir şeye ve hiç kimseye muhtaç değildir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:15/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:15/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:15/r2.claim: God alone deserves praise because of His superior blessings upon created beings.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:15/r2.anchor: yaratılmışlar üzerindeki üstün nimetlerinden ötürü hamdedilmeye lâyık olan yalnız O’dur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:15/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:15/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:15/r3.claim: Humanity needs worship; religious feeling and the inclination to worship God are innate and cannot be eliminated through coercion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:15/r3.anchor: insanın ibadete ihtiyacı olduğu, dolayısıyla din duygusunun ve Allah’a ibadet etme eğiliminin fıtrî olduğu ve baskı yöntemleriyle yok edilmesinin mümkün olmadığı anlaşılmaktadır.

QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r2.claim: There are two kinds of poverty: essential poverty of created nature and poverty as a spiritual quality.
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r2.anchor: الفقر على ضربين : فقر الخلقة وفقر الصفة

QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r3.claim: Essential poverty is universal: every creature needs its Creator to bring it from nonbeing into existence and then to sustain and preserve it.
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r3.anchor: فكل مخلوق مفتقر إلى خالقه ، فهو قد حصل من العدم ، فهو مفتقر إليه ليبديه وينشيه

QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r4.claim: Poverty as a spiritual quality is detachment: ordinary people detach from wealth, while the elect detach from impediments so that their poverty may be sound.
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r4.anchor: وأما فقر الصفة فهو التجرد ، ففقر العوام التجرد من المال ، وفقر الخواص التجرد من الأعلال

QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r5.claim: People may be needy toward God or toward something that comes from God; dependence on a thing is a kind of self-sufficiency through that thing, while need of God is richness through God, and each entails the other.
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r5.anchor: ومن افتقر إلى شيء استغنى بوجود ذلك الشيء ؛ فالفقير إلى الله هو الغني بالله

QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r6.claim: Poverty is ennobled by humility and submission, while wealth can be marred by pride; the servant’s honor lies in poverty and abasement in imagining oneself self-sufficient.
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r6.anchor: ومن شرف الفقر اقترانه بالتواضع والخضوع ، ومن آفات الغنى امتزاجه بالتكبر

QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r7.claim: Blameworthy poverty is when God veils a person from seeing where they need Him; praiseworthy poverty is when God makes those places of need visible.
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r7.anchor: ومن الفقر المذموم ، أن يستر الحق على صاحبه مواضع فقره إلى ربه ، ومن الفقر المحمود أن يشهده الحق مواضع فقره إليه

QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r8.claim: The sincere poor person owns nothing yet owns everything; more precisely, no thing possesses the truly poor person.
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r8.anchor: ومن شرط الفقير المخلص ألا يملك شيئا ويملك كل شيء . ويقال : الفقير الصادق الذي لا يملكه شيء

QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r9.claim: The sincere poor person’s courtesy is to show gratitude at the height of being broken.
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r9.anchor: ومن آداب الفقير الصادق إظهار التشكر عند كمال التكسر

QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r10.claim: The etiquette of poverty is completeness of spiritual meaning and the disappearance of self-claim.
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r10.anchor: ومن آداب الفقر كمال المعنى وزوال الدعوى

QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r11.claim: Another practice is to be grateful in affliction and refrain from complaint.
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r11.anchor: ويقال الشكر على البلوى والبعد عن الشكوى

QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r12.claim: The reality of praiseworthy poverty is stripping the innermost self of causal attachments and making the heart exclusively God’s.
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r12.anchor: وحقيقة الفقر المحمود تجرد السر عن المعلولات وإفراد القلب بالله

QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r13.claim: Praiseworthy poverty is living with God in the ease of an unoccupied inward state throughout time, without resisting any condition.
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r13.anchor: ويقال : الفقر المحمود العيش مع الله براحة الفراغ على سرمد الوقت من غير استكراه شيء منه

QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r14.claim: God’s self-description as rich and praiseworthy signals that He gives until He is praised.
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r14.anchor: الإشارة منه أن يعطي حتى يحمد

QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r15.claim: Created beings display wealth either to boast or outdo others, or to give generously; God is far above the first motives, so His declaration of human poverty signals generosity rather than belittlement.
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r15.anchor: وإنما المقصود أنه إذا قال : والله الغني ، وأنتم الفقراء أنه يجود علينا

QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r16.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r16.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r16.claim: If one does not claim self-sufficiency, which belongs to God, God grants what enriches and gives beyond what is sufficient.
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r16.anchor: ويقال إذا لم تدع ما هو صفته - من استحقاق الغنى - أولاك ما يغنيك ، وأعطاك فوق ما يكفيك

BURHAN:v2p144/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p144/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURHAN:v2p144/r4.claim: The Prophet says the upper hand is better than the lower; the lower hand is the receiver and the upper the giver, with the loan verse offered as support.
BURHAN:v2p144/r4.anchor: وقوله اليد العليا خير من اليد السفلى

BURHAN:v2p144/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p144/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p144/r5.claim: The giver's charity depends on a recipient accepting the due owed to God, which purifies the giver; without a receiving hand, the wealthy could not give charity.
BURHAN:v2p144/r5.anchor: أن العطية من أيدينا مفتقرة إلى من يضع فيها حقا وجب عليها

ITQAN:v3p222#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p222#2/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p222#2/r4.claim: A vocative can stand without a following command, introducing a statement such as people’s dependence on God or Abraham’s question to his father.
ITQAN:v3p222#2/r4.anchor: وقد لا تعقبها نحو ﴿ يا عباد لا خوف عليكم اليوم ﴾ ﴿ يا أيها الناس أنتم الفقراء إلى الله ﴾

SULAMI:v2p158#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r1.claim: Sahl says God declared Himself rich and creation poor: claiming self-sufficiency veils one, while manifesting need to God joins poverty to His richness.
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r1.anchor: قال سهل : لما خلق الله تعالى الخلق حكم لنفسه بالغناء ولهم بالفقر فمن ادعى الغناء حجب عن الله

SULAMI:v2p158#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r2.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r2.claim: He says genuine poverty appears in primordial need, present dependence, and relinquishing one’s own management; otherwise the claim of poverty is false.
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r2.anchor: ويصح إظهار الفقر في ثلاثة ، فقرهم القديم ، وفقرهم في حالهم ، وفقرهم في موت أنفسهم من تدبيرهم

SULAMI:v2p158#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r3.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r3.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh prefers poverty because it brings humility while wealth fosters pride; returning humbly to God is better than approaching with many deeds.
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r3.anchor: قال يحيى بن معاذ : الفقر خير للعبد من الغنى لأن المذلة في الفقر والكبر مع الغنى

SULAMI:v2p158#4/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r4.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r4.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī says whoever becomes rich through God does not lack, and whoever is empowered through Him is not humiliated.
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r4.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : من استغنى بالله لا يفتقر ، ومن تعزز بالله لا يذل

SULAMI:v2p158#4/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r5.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r5.claim: Al-Ḥusayn says the servant’s poverty toward God corresponds to richness through Him, need of Him, and returning to Him in every matter.
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r5.anchor: قال الحسين : على مقدار افتقار العبد إلى الله يكون غناه بالله في كل شيء والفقر إليه في كل شيء والرجوع إليه في كل شيء

SULAMI:v2p158#4/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r6.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r6.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī calls the one who conceals the Real’s due the poorest, and the one who lays that due bare before Him the truly rich.
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r6.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : افقر الفقراء من ستر الحق حقيقة حقه والغنى من كاشف الحق حقيقة حقه له

SULAMI:v2p158#4/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r7.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r7.claim: Sahl says people need God in every breath; the servant should inwardly depend on Him and sever reliance on all else, since servanthood is need, abasement, and submission.
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r7.anchor: قال سهل رحمة الله عليه : أنتم الفقراء إليه في كل نفس ، ينبغي للعبد أن يكون مفتقرا إليه بالسر ومنقطعا إليه من غيره

SULAMI:v2p158#4/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r8.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r8.claim: Al-Junayd contrasts divine lordship—knowledge, power, dominion, and will—with servanthood’s incapacity, need, weakness, and inability to escape necessity.
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r8.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمة الله عليه : قد عجزت عن علم العبودية كيف تدرك علم الربوبية

SULAMI:v2p158#4/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r9.speaker: ذو النون
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r9.claim: Dhū al-Nūn says creatures need God in every breath, thought, and moment.
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r9.anchor: قال ذو النون رحمة الله عليه : الخلق محتاجون إليه في كل نفس وخطرة ولحظة

SULAMI:v2p158#4/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r10.speaker: محمد بن عبد الوهاب
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r10.claim: In a report, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb calls poverty God’s secret, not entrusted to one who discloses it, because God suffices and enriches His friends.
SULAMI:v2p158#4/r10.anchor: رأيت محمد بن عبد الوهاب فقال لي : يا أبا القاسم ايش أنت فقلت أنا الفقير فقال الفقر سر الله لا يودعه من يظهره

SULAMI:v2p159/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p159/r1.speaker: الجوزجاني
SULAMI:v2p159/r1.claim: Al-Jūzjānī calls poverty and need the abode of protection, whose gate is recognizing divine favor.
SULAMI:v2p159/r1.anchor: وقال الجوزجاني : الفقر والفاقة دار العصمة وبابها معرفة المنة

SULAMI:v2p159/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p159/r2.speaker: الشبلي
SULAMI:v2p159/r2.claim: Al-Shiblī describes poverty as an ocean of affliction whose every affliction is honor.
SULAMI:v2p159/r2.anchor: وقال الشبلي : الفقر بحر البلاء وبلاؤه كله عز

SULAMI:v2p159/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p159/r3.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p159/r3.claim: Al-Junayd says God made creation poor to Him while needing nothing from them, proving that all things depend on Him and He is independent of all.
SULAMI:v2p159/r3.anchor: وقال الجنيد رحمة الله عليه : خلق الخلق وأفقره إليه بغناه عنهم فقال : ﴿ أنتم الفقراء إلى الله ﴾ ثم قال : ﴿ والله هو الغني الحميد ﴾

SULAMI:v2p159/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p159/r4.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p159/r4.claim: Asked whether need of God or being enriched through Him is more complete, al-Junayd says sound need completes richness through God; neither state is complete without the other.
SULAMI:v2p159/r4.anchor: فقال : إذا صح الافتقار إلى الله كمل الغنى بالله ، ولا يقال أيهما أتم لانهما حالان لا يتم أحدهما إلا بالآخر

SULAMI:v2p159/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p159/r5.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p159/r5.claim: Al-Junayd says poverty and richness each belong to servanthood.
SULAMI:v2p159/r5.anchor: سمعت الجنيد رحمة الله عليه وعليهم يقول في قوله : ﴿ أنتم الفقراء إلى الله ﴾ فقال : الفقر يليق بالعبودية والغنى يليق بالعبودية

SULAMI:v2p159/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p159/r6.speaker: سعد
SULAMI:v2p159/r6.claim: Saʿd says the truthful poor person neither asks, stores, nor withholds.
SULAMI:v2p159/r6.anchor: قال سعد : الفقير الصادق لا يسأل ولا يدخر ولا يحبس

SULAMI:v2p159/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p159/r7.speaker: الخواص
SULAMI:v2p159/r7.claim: Al-Khawwāṣ says true poverty is marked by leaving complaint and concealing the traces of affliction.
SULAMI:v2p159/r7.anchor: سئل الخواص ما علامة الفقر الصادق ؟ قال : ترك الشكوى وأخفاء اثر البلوي

SULAMI:v2p159/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p159/r8.speaker: رويم
SULAMI:v2p159/r8.claim: Ruwaym describes poverty as having no possession and entering into things for another’s sake, not one’s own.
SULAMI:v2p159/r8.anchor: وسئل رويم عن الفقر ؟ فقال : عدم كل موجود ويكون في الأشياء دخوله لغيره لا له

SULAMI:v2p159/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p159/r9.speaker: بشر بن الحارث
SULAMI:v2p159/r9.claim: Bishr ibn al-Ḥārith calls poverty a hidden treasure for the believer, like martyrdom, granted only to those God loves.
SULAMI:v2p159/r9.anchor: سمعت بشر بن الحارث يقول : الفقر مخزون مكنون للمؤمن مثل الشهادة لا ينالها إلا من احبه الله من عباده

SULAMI:v2p159/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p159/r10.speaker: أبو سعيد الخراز
SULAMI:v2p159/r10.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Kharrāz defines true poverty as taking little and choosing less over more when in need.
SULAMI:v2p159/r10.anchor: قال أبو سعيد الخراز : حقيقة الفقر اخذ شيء منه واختيار القليل على الكثير عند الحاجة

SULAMI:v2p159/r11.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p159/r11.speaker: إبراهيم بن أدهم
SULAMI:v2p159/r11.claim: Ibrāhīm ibn Adham says patience with poverty is what led him into it.
SULAMI:v2p159/r11.anchor: وقيل : لإبراهيم بن ادهم رحمة الله عليه ما الذي ورثك الدخول في الفقر ؟ . قال : الصبر عليه

SULAMI:v2p159/r12.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p159/r12.speaker: عمرو المكي
SULAMI:v2p159/r12.claim: ʿAmr al-Makkī says poverty appears outwardly as affliction but inwardly is blessing; because reward is promised, the servant should manifest the inner blessing and conceal the visible trial.
SULAMI:v2p159/r12.anchor: قال عمرو المكي : الفقر ظاهرة ظاهر البلوى وباطنه باطن النعمة وقد وقع عليه كريم الوعد بالجزاء

TUSTARI:35:15/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:35:15/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:35:15/r1.claim: God created people as needy before Him while He is rich; claiming self-sufficiency veils one from God, while manifesting need joins one's poverty to His wealth.
TUSTARI:35:15/r1.anchor: فمن ادعى الغنى حجب عن الله عز وجل، ومن أظهر فقره إليه أوصل الله فقره بغناه

TUSTARI:35:15/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:35:15/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:35:15/r2.claim: The servant should inwardly need God and sever dependence on all else for pure servanthood, whose essence is abasement and humility.
TUSTARI:35:15/r2.anchor: ينبغي للعبد أن يكون مفتقرا إليه في السر، منقطعا عن غيره، حتى تكون عبوديته محضة

TUSTARI:35:15/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:35:15/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:35:15/r3.claim: True need is shown through primordial need, present need, and the death of the self's own management; otherwise the claimed poverty is false.
TUSTARI:35:15/r3.anchor: قال: إظهار الفقر في ثلاث: فقرهم القديم، وفقرهم في حالهم، وفقرهم في موت أنفسهم

TUSTARI:35:15/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:35:15/r4.speaker: author
TUSTARI:35:15/r4.claim: The truthful poor person neither asks, refuses, nor withholds.
TUSTARI:35:15/r4.anchor: الفقير الصادق الذي لا يسأل ولا يرد ولا يحبس

TUSTARI:35:15/r5.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:35:15/r5.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
TUSTARI:35:15/r5.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz describes God's friends by trust in Him in everything, need of Him in everything, and return to Him from everything.
TUSTARI:35:15/r5.anchor: وقال عمر بن عبد العزيز رضي الله عنه: صفة أولياء الله عز وجل ثلاثة أشياء

NAHHAS:v3p367/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p367/r8.speaker: الخليل
NAHHAS:v3p367/r8.claim: Al-Khalīl considers easing the second hamza in al-fuqarāʾ the best option; also permitted are easing or dropping the first, easing both, or pronouncing both clearly.
NAHHAS:v3p367/r8.anchor: بتخفيف الهمزة الثانية أجود الوجوه عند الخليل رحمه الله ويجوز تخفيف الأولى وحذفها

NAHHAS:v3p367/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p367/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p367/r9.claim: Huwa may be an extra particle without a syntactic position or a nominative subject.
NAHHAS:v3p367/r9.anchor: تكون هو زائدة فلا يكون لها موضع من الإعراب وتكون مبتدأ فيكون موضعها رفعا

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p366/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p366/r3.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p366/r3.claim: Al-Raghib defines bu's, ba's, and ba'sa as hardship, with bu's especially in poverty and war and ba's/ba'sa in attack; the author objects that Qur'anic ba'sa pairs with adversity, not attack.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p366/r3.anchor: قول "الراغب" في (المفردات) : "البؤس والبأس والبأساء، الشدة والمكروه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p366/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p366/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p366/r4.claim: Against al-Raghib's association of bu's with poverty, the Qur'an explicitly contrasts faqr with divine wealth in four verses.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p366/r4.anchor: أن القرآن يستعمل الفقر مقابل الغنى بصريح آيات

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p366/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p366/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p366/r5.claim: The Qur'an uses ba's, rather than bu's, for warfare, fighting, force, and dominance.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p366/r5.anchor: وكذلك يأتي البأس، لا البؤس، في الحرب والقتال وفي الجبروت والسطوة، بصريح آيات

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p334/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p334/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p334/r6.claim: The call benefits people, who need God while He needs nothing from them; acceptance brings success in both worlds and rejection brings ruin.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p334/r6.anchor: God does not need them; on the contrary, they need God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p343/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p343/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p343/r5.claim: Verses 15-17 intensify the preceding admonition and address everyone; the Messenger's tireless efforts to awaken people do not mean God needs their response.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p343/r5.anchor: so that everyone should fully listen up that all this elaborate arrangement made for their education and reminding

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p343/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p343/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p343/r6.claim: God is wholly self-sufficient and praiseworthy in His attributes, while people need Him in this world and the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p343/r6.anchor: and praiseworthy in His attributes; it is these people who need God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r1.claim: God is perfect and complete, with no dependence on anything outside Himself; His relationship with creation rests on mercy and favor, not need.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r1.anchor: God’s being is perfect and complete and this perfection of His is not dependent on anything external to His being.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r2.claim: An unattributed Persian couplet says God created people to show generosity and mercy, not to gain any benefit for Himself.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r2.anchor: I did not create [people] to receive benefit for Myself; in fact, I created them to show them mercy

NASHR:v1p387/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p387/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p387/r2.claim: The fifth class has a ḍamma then kasra and 22 agreed occurrences, including ولا يأب الشهداء إذا and الفقراء إلى الله; six occurrences differ, including Maryam’s يا ذكرياء إنا and five addresses to the Prophet attributed to Nafi.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r1.claim: People need God for their existence and every important matter; the definite plural intensifies their pervasive need, making other creatures' need seem negligible.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r1.anchor: في أنفسكم وفيما يعن لكم من أمر مهم أو خطب ملم

ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r2.claim: Human weakness supports this reading; jinn need less for food and clothing and are not weak in the same way, so need not be included.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r2.anchor: ولا يرد الجن إذ هم لا يحتاجون في المطعم والملبس وغيرهما كما يحتاج الإنسان

ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r3.claim: Even if jinn are excluded, the address may target people who display strength and stubbornness; restricting poverty to comparison with God is unpersuasive.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r3.anchor: إذ الكلام مع من يظهر القوة والعناد من الناس والقول أن القصر إضافي بالنسبة إليه تعالى لا يخفى ما فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r4.speaker: صاحب الفرائد
ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r4.claim: The author of al-Fara'id includes humans and other beings, using the present over the absent and the superior over others; al-Alusi calls this very remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r4.anchor: صاحب الفرائد : الوجه أن يقال والله تعالى أعلم المراد الناس وغيرهم

ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r5.speaker: العلامة الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r5.claim: Al-Tibi reads people as a contextual reference to those addressed in 35:13, and poverty generically: they are the creatures most in need of God; al-Alusi finds this appealing.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r5.anchor: الذي يقتضيه النظم الجليل أن يحمل التعريف في الناس على العهد وفي الفقراء على الجنس

ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r6.claim: God alone is free of need and is benefactor of all beings, deserving praise for His beneficence; hamid originally means praised.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r6.anchor: المنعم على جميع الموجودات المستحق بأنعامه سبحانه للحمد وأصله المحمود

ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r7.claim: Calling God Praiseworthy completes the account of human need: wealth benefits the needy only when its owner is generous and beneficent.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r7.anchor: وأريد به ذلك على طريق الكناية ليناسب ذكره بعد فقرهم إذ الغني لا ينفع الفقير إلا إذا كان جوادا منعما

ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r8.claim: Ka'b al-Ghanawi's line about a forbearing man respected by an enemy illustrates the praiseworthy sense of hamid.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r8.anchor: قول كعب الغنوي : حليم إذا ما الحلم زين أهله

ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r9.speaker: العلامة الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r9.claim: Al-Tibi says God is independent of the addressees and their worship, since other servants praise Him; al-Alusi prefers the broader reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p183/r9.anchor: وهو سبحانه غني عنكم وعن عبادتكم

ALUSI-FULL:v22p184/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184/r1.claim: A reported occasion says that after the Prophet prayed persistently and unbelievers persisted in rejection, they wondered whether God needed their worship; the verse was revealed in response.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184/r1.anchor: وما روى في سبب النزول من أنه لما كثر من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الدعاء

ALUSI-FULL:v22p184/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184/r2.claim: That reported occasion does not require narrowing the verse to that circumstance.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184/r2.anchor: لا يقتضي شيئا من التخصيص في الآية كما لا يخفى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r6.claim: People are needy for God's favor; a faqir is one who is in need.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r7.claim: God has no need of His creation and is praised for His beneficence toward them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r7.anchor: الغني عن خلقه المحمود في إحسانه إليهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r1.claim: People need God in their very selves and in everything that befalls them; the definite plural intensifies their dependence, which is so great that other creatures' need scarcely counts by comparison.
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r1.anchor: وتعريف الفقراء للمبالغة في فقرهم كأنهم لشدة افتقارهم وكثرة احتياجهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r2.claim: God is absolutely self-sufficient and benefits all beings, so He deserves their praise.
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r2.anchor: المستغني على الإطلاق المنعم على سائر الموجودات حتى استحق عليهم الحمد

BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r9.claim: All people are dependent on God: their extensive knowledge, thought, and intellect multiply their competing needs, while their weakness and incapacity make other creatures' need seem negligible.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r9.anchor: لاتساع معارفكم وسريان أفكاركم وانتشار عقولكم تكثر نوازغكم وتتفرق دواعيكم فيعظم احتياجكم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r10.claim: The definite predicate al-fuqarāʾ conveys this particular, encompassing poverty; an indefinite predicate would not express the same force.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r10.anchor: ولو نكر الخبر لم يفد هذا المعنى

BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r11.speaker: القشيري
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r11.claim: Al-Qushayri distinguishes universal created poverty, dependence on God to originate and sustain, from poverty as detachment; commoners detach from wealth, the elect from causes, and true praiseworthy poverty is detachment of the heart from effects.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r11.anchor: قال القشيري : والفقر على ضربين : فقر خلقة , وفقر صفة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r12.claim: God alone is absolutely self-sufficient: He needs neither people, their worship, nor anything whatsoever.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r12.anchor: أي الذي لا يتصور أن يحتاج لا إليكم ولا إلى عبادتكم ولا إلى شيء أصلا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r13.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r13.claim: Al-Harali defines praise as the perfection of a whole when every part and matter reaches its full end; a deficient part prevents the whole from being wholly praiseworthy.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r13.anchor: وكان الحمد كما قال الحرالي في شرح الأسماء : حسن الكلية بانتهاء كل أمر وجزء , وبعض منها إلى غاية تمامه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r14.claim: God creates everything fittingly and at its appointed measure, without haste; blame arises from viewing parts in isolation rather than seeing the whole.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r14.anchor: وكان الله قد خلق كل شيء كما ينبغي , لم يعجل شيئا عن إناه وقدره , وكان الذم استنقاضا يلحق بعض الأجزاء

BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r15.speaker: الغزالي
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r15.claim: Al-Ghazali defines a praiseworthy human as one whose habits, character, and deeds are all praised without exception.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r15.anchor: ولذلك قال الغزالي : الحميد من العباد من حمدت عوائده وأخلاقه وأعماله كلها من غير مثنوية

BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r16.claim: Unlike created wealth, which cannot satisfy all who seek it and is constrained by fear or other limits, God's gifts are unrestricted and His praise is complete.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r16.anchor: الغنى من الخلق لا يسع غناه من يقصده , وإن وسعهم لم يسعهم عطاؤه لخوف الفقر

BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r17.claim: God has poured out visible and hidden blessings and enabled people to receive them; His gifts are not barred, as the cited verse says.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r17.anchor: أسبغها ظاهرة وباطنة , وجعل لهم قدرة على تناولها . لا يعوق عنه إلا قدرته ( وما كان عطاء ربك محظورا )

BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r18.claim: God's giving and withholding are both praiseworthy: neither serves a self-interested aim, but follows wisdom too subtle for minds to grasp.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r18.anchor: كان إعطاؤه حمدا ومنعه حمدا , لأنه لا يكون مانعا لغرض بل لحكمة تدق عن الأفكار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r8.claim: After abundant proofs and reminders fail to move the people and may feed their arrogance, the next address stresses God’s independence and that Islam will gain adherents who honor it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r8.anchor: ناسب أن ينبئهم الله بأنه غني عنهم وأن دينه لا يعتز بأمثالهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p285/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p285/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p285/r1.claim: ‘People’ refers here to the polytheists, as is common Qur’anic usage, and to those addressed in the preceding passage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p285/r1.anchor: فالمراد ب { يا أيها الناس } هم المشركون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p285/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p285/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p285/r2.claim: Reminding them first of their dependence on God humbles them more than simply telling them He needs nothing from them; although they know their dependence, they miss its implications, so the reminder may awaken or convince them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p285/r2.anchor: وجه إليهم إعلام بأنهم الفقراء إلى الله لأن ذلك أدخل للذلة على عظمتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p285/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p285/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p285/r3.claim: The reminder may revive people whose sound minds were veiled by misguidance; even those remaining unbelievers will meet their lives with bewilderment and bitterness, unlike the praise of their ancestors and idols they had heard.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p285/r3.anchor: فمن بقي على كفره كان بقاؤه مشوبا بحيرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p285/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p285/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p285/r4.claim: The defined subject and predicate restrict poverty to the addressed people relative to God, a restrictive reversal; Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects a literal absolute restriction or an asserted hyperbolic reading as needless.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p285/r4.anchor: فالوجه حمل القصر المستفاد من جملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p285/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p285/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p285/r5.claim: Adding al-Ḥamīd completes al-Ghanī and prevents the inference that divine independence excuses failure to worship; God is praised by those who worship and answer His call.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p285/r5.anchor: فهو احتراس لدفع توهمهم أنه لما كان غنيا عن استجابتهم وعبادتهم فهم معذورون في أن لا يعبدوه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p285/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p285/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p285/r6.claim: The wording balances their need ‘to God’ with His praise, and pairs their poverty with His wealth to show that divine wealth is joined to generosity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p285/r6.anchor: لأنه لما قيد فقرهم بالكون إلى الله قيد غنى الله تعالى بوصف { الحميد }

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r1.claim: Humanity depends on God in both small and great matters and cannot dispense with Him for even an instant; through Him, each person can dispense with everyone else.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r1.anchor: والإنسان فقير إلى الله تعالى في دقائق الأمور وجلائلها لا يستغني عنه طرفة عين، وهو به مستغن عن كل واحد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r2.claim: God is absolutely self-sufficient from people and every created thing, and absolutely praiseworthy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r2.anchor: والله تعالى غني عن الناس وعن كل شيء من مخلوقاته غني على الإطلاق، والحميد المحمود بالإطلاق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p435/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p435/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p435/r1.claim: No expression fully conveys the eloquence of this verse, as with the whole Qur'an; the eloquence is more apparent in some passages according to our shortcomings.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p435/r1.anchor: وكل عبارة مقصرة عن تبيين فصاحة هذه الآية، وكذلك كتاب الله كله، ولكن يظهر الأمر لنا نحن في مواضع أكثر منه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482/r1.claim: People are in need of God, who needs nothing from their worship and is praiseworthy among creation for His beneficence toward them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482/r1.anchor: أي المحتاجون إليه والله هو الغني عن عبادتكم الحميد عند خلقه بإحسانه إليهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p541#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p541#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p541#2/r1.claim: All creatures need God in every movement and stillness, while He is inherently independent of them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p541#2/r1.anchor: هم محتاجون إليه في جميع الحركات والسكنات، وهو الغني عنهم بالذات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p541#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p541#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p541#2/r2.claim: God alone possesses wealth without partner and is praiseworthy in everything He does, says, decrees, and legislates.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p541#2/r2.anchor: بالغنى وحده لا شريك له، وهو الحميد في جميع ما يفعله ويقوله، ويقدره ويشرعه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615#2/r1.claim: The definite form presents people as the class of the needy because their weakness makes their dependence acute; an indefinite form would mean merely some needy people.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615#2/r1.anchor: قصد بذلك أن يريهم أنهم لشدة افتقارهم إليه هم جنس الفقراء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615#2/r2.claim: Human weakness underlies this intensified need, as affirmed by the verses saying humanity was created weak and created from weakness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615#2/r2.anchor: وقد شهد الله سبحانه على الإنسان بالضعف في قوله : { وخلق الإنسان ضعيفا }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615#2/r3.claim: حميد adds that wealth alone benefits no one unless its possessor is generous and beneficent; recipients then praise their benefactor, who merits praise.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615#2/r3.anchor: وليس كل غني نافعا بغناه إلا إذا كان الغني جوادا منعما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615#2/r4.claim: In the following verse, بعزيز means beyond God's power or impossible for Him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615#2/r4.anchor: بممتنع ، وهذا غضب عليهم لاتخاذهم له أندادا

MUQATIL:35:15-19/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:35:15-19/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:35:15-19/r1.claim: The people addressed are Meccan unbelievers, needy of what God has; God has no need of their worship and is praised by His creation.
MUQATIL:35:15-19/r1.anchor: { يأيها الناس } يعني كفار مكة { أنتم الفقراء إلى الله } يعني إلى ما عند الله تعالى { والله هو الغني } عن عبادتكم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r1.speaker: ذو النون
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r1.claim: Dhu al-Nūn says creatures need God in every breath, thought, and moment, because their existence and continuance depend on Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r1.anchor: قال ذو النون الخلق محتاجون إليه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r2.claim: People are called poor not to demean them but to direct them toward dependence; God is independent of all things.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r2.anchor: ولم يسمهم بالفقراء للتحقير بل للتعريض على الاستغناء ولهذا وصف نفسه بالغنى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r3.claim: God is praised by every tongue; His riches benefit creation because He gives generously, and beneficiaries praise their benefactor.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r3.anchor: المحمود بكل لسان ولم يسمهم بالفقراء للتحقير بل للتعريض على الاستغناء

NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r4.speaker: سهل
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r4.claim: Sahl says self-sufficiency veils a person, while displaying need brings one to God; inward dependence and cutting off from others make servitude pure, whose sign is asking no one.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r4.anchor: قال سهل لما خلق الله الخلق حكم لنفسه بالغنى ولهم بالفقر فمن ادعى الغنى حجب عن الله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r5.speaker: الواسطى
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r5.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī says whoever finds sufficiency through God is not poor, and whoever is ennobled through God is not abased.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r5.anchor: وقال الواسطى من استغنى بالله لا يفتقر ومن تعزز بالله لا يذل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r6.speaker: الحسين
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r6.claim: Al-Ḥusayn says God-given richness corresponds to need: the more dependent a servant becomes, the richer he becomes.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r6.anchor: وقال الحسين على مقدار افتقار العبد إلى الله يكون غنيا بالله وكلما ازداد افتقارا ازداد غنى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r7.speaker: يحيى
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r7.claim: Yaḥyā says poverty is better than wealth because it brings humility and wealth pride; returning humbly to God is better than returning with multiplied deeds.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r7.anchor: وقال يحيى الفقر خير للعبد من الغنى لأن المذلة فى الفقر والكبر فى الغنى والرجوع إلى الله بالتواضع

NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r8.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r8.claim: One view lists three marks of saints: trust in God, need of Him, and returning to Him, each in everything.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r8.anchor: وقيل صفة الأولياء ثلاثة الثقة بالله في كل شيء والفقر إليه في كل شيء والرجوع إليه من كل شىء

NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r9.speaker: الشبلى
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r9.claim: Al-Shiblī says poverty draws affliction, and all the affliction it brings is honor.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#3/r9.anchor: وقال الشبلى الفقر يجر البلاء وبلاؤه كله عز

QURTUBI-FULL:35:15/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:15/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:15/r1.claim: People need God for their continued existence and in every circumstance.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:15/r1.anchor: أي المحتاجون إليه في بقائكم وكل أحوالكم. الزمخشري: «فإن قلت لم عرف الفقراء

QURTUBI-FULL:35:15/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:15/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:35:15/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the definite “the needy” as showing that people, through the severity of their need and weakness, constitute the class of the needy, though all creatures depend on God; an indefinite form would mean only some needy people.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:15/r2.anchor: قصد بذلك أن يريهم أنهم لشدة افتقارهم إليه هم جنس الفقراء، وإن كانت الخلائق كلهم مفتقرين

QURTUBI-FULL:35:15/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:15/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:35:15/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says “the Praiseworthy” adds that wealth alone does not benefit others: God is generous and beneficent through His wealth, so recipients owe Him praise.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:15/r3.anchor: لما أثبت فقرهم إليه وغناه عنهم، وليس كل غني نافعا بغناه إلا إذا كان الغني جوادا منعما

QURTUBI-FULL:35:15/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:15/r4.speaker: الخليل
QURTUBI-FULL:35:15/r4.claim: Al-Khalil considers easing the second of the two hamzas the best pronunciation; easing only the first, easing both, or pronouncing both fully are also allowed.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:15/r4.anchor: وتخفيف الهمزة الثانية أجود الوجوه عند الخليل، ويجوز تخفيف الأولى وحدها

QURTUBI-FULL:35:15/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:15/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:15/r5.claim: “Huwa” may be an extra particle with no syntactic position, or the beginning of a nominal sentence and thus nominative.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:15/r5.anchor: تكون «هو» زائدة، فلا يكون لها موضع من الإعراب، وتكون مبتدأة فيكون موضعها رفعا
